version.changelog:
SkillUp v0.1.4

- Added detailed SKILL.md documentation covering usage, input options, and publish flow.
- Supports publishing to GitHub, 虾评 Skill, OpenClaw 中文社区, and ClawHub with environment variable–first credential strategy.
- Provides shell entrypoint for skill checking, packaging, and multi-platform publishing without relying on browser automation.
- Includes dry-run, error handling, and configurable platform targeting.
- Added support for publishing entire skills repositories and for per-platform enable/disable via manifest.
- Output includes machine-readable results for automation scenarios.

llm.summary: The skill's code, declared requirements, and runtime instructions are consistent with a multi-target skill-publishing tool; no obvious misdirection or malicious behavior found, but review required credentials and target endpoints before use.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (publish skills to GitHub, Xiaping, OpenClaw, ClawHub) align with the required binaries (curl, git, gh, claw, clawhub) and environment variables; included shell scripts implement the expected packaging and platform-specific publish flows.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and scripts instruct the agent to run the included shell scripts which: read optional config files, package skill directories, invoke platform CLIs (gh/claw/clawhub), and POST artifacts to configured HTTP endpoints. They create temporary logs and response files under /tmp. This behavior is expected for a publisher, but the skill will make network requests and invoke CLIs — review endpoints (xiaping.coze.site, clawhub.ai, any configured base_url) and logs if you need to trust destination servers.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Instruction-only skill with shipped shell scripts; there is no external download or installer. Nothing is pulled from arbitrary URLs at install time.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Requested credentials (GitHub token, Xiaping API key, OpenClaw and ClawHub tokens) are relevant to publishing. Minor inconsistency: SKILL.md and scripts use a CLAWHUB_TOKEN fallback but the registry's requires.env list does not include CLAWHUB_TOKEN — the skill will accept CLAWHUB_TOKEN in the environment as an alternate. Ensure any tokens provided are scoped to the minimal permissions needed (repo/release and publish APIs) before installing.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill does not request permanent system-wide presence. It will export tokens into subprocess environments temporarily (e.g., GH_TOKEN, CLAWHUB_TOKEN) and may modify remote resources (create/push repos, create releases) as part of its intended purpose.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to be what it says: a cross-platform publisher that runs the included shell scripts, calls CLIs (gh, claw, clawhub) and posts artifacts to configured endpoints. Before installing: (1) Review and prefer a dry-run (--dry-run) to see actions without network publishes. (2) Only supply API tokens with the least privileges necessary (e.g., GitHub token scoped to repos/releases you intend to use). (3) Inspect config.example.toml and any configured base_url values to confirm you trust endpoints such as https://xiaping.coze.site and https://clawhub.ai or override them to known endpoints. (4) Note the skill writes logs and temporary response files under /tmp and writes artifacts to the artifact-dir; ensure those locations are acceptable. (5) Be aware the scripts may create or push to repositories when configured to do so (gh repo create, git push). If you need higher assurance, review the scripts in this package (they are all plain shell + small Python helpers) or run them in an isolated environment first.
